title: dedicated: refactor autoscaler backpressure path and improve utilization reporting
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: dedicated fleets can hit transient overloads that cause degraded tail latency and incorrect utilization signals. This PR refactors the autoscaler backpressure path to detach throttling decision logic from the placement loop, introduces a smoother token-bucket based throttle smoothing, and extends utilization reporting with new aggregated metrics so fleet autoscaler decisions are based on stable, debounced signals. Changes include: 1) move backpressure decision code into autoscaler/backpressure.go, 2) add a token-bucket smoother (configurable window and alpha) to reduce oscillation, 3) publish new Prometheus metrics dedicated_autoscaler_backpressure_active, dedicated_autoscaler_backpressure_throttle_ratio, and dedicated_autoscaler_allocated_utilization, 4) fix a race where stale per-node utilization was returned under high update rates (root cause: concurrent map access in utilization cache), 5) update the reporting pipeline to emit bucketed utilization histograms for per-fleet rollups. This is a refactor + feature PR: performance-sensitive code has microbenchmarks and unit/e2e coverage. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated (ENG-2123) - [x] unit tests for backpressure logic - [x] microbenchmarks added for token-bucket smoother - [x] e2e test for utilization reporting under load - [x] docs/observability notes added - [x] metrics reviewed by SRE Notes: default smoothing params are conservative to avoid sudden throttling; fleet owners can tune via DedicatedAutoscalerConfig. Related: PRs that previously added util reporting vN and tokenbucket smoothing.
